**A [[Rwanda]]n [[United Nations]] [[Peacekeeping|peacekeeper]] was killed and two others wounded in an [[ambush]] on a convoy in [[Nana-Mambéré]], [[Central African Republic]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/07/car-rebel-ambush-kills-peacekeeper-injured-200714135038697.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Arts and culture
*[[Removal of Confederate monuments and memorials]]
**The [[University of Mississippi]] removes a monument of [[Confederate States Army|Confederate]] soldiers from the campus. The monument is expected to be relocated to a cemetery. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/nbcblk/university-mississippi-removes-confederate-statue-heart-campus-n1233782 (NBC News)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Iran explosions]]
**[[Government of Iran|Iranian]] [[Law Enforcement Force (Iran)|police]] launch an investigation following another suspicious [[explosion]], this one at an industrial complex south of [[Mashhad]]. [https://www.al-monitor.com/pulse/originals/2020/07/iran-fire-kavian-industrial-mashhad-nuclear-sites-explosion.html (Al-Monitor)]
*The fire on [[USS Bonhomme Richard (LHD-6)|USS ''Bonhomme Richard'']] continues for a third consecutive day. The [[United States Navy]] says its crews have made significant progress fighting flames and reducing smoke, but it is still unclear when the fire will be extinguished. There have been 61 injuries; 38 sailors and 23 civilians have been treated mostly for minor injuries related to firefighting. [https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/news/military/story/2020-07-14/navy-says-crew-made-progress-on-still-burning-ship-fire (''The San Diego Union-Tribune'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)|COVID-19 pandemic in New York]]
****[[Governor of New York|New York Governor]] [[Andrew Cuomo]] adds [[Minnesota]], [[New Mexico]], [[Ohio]] and [[Wisconsin]] to the state's quarantine requirement list, while [[Delaware]] is removed. [https://thehill.com/homenews/state-watch/507245-new-york-adds-four-new-states-to-quarantine-requirement-list (''The Hill'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Virginia]]
****[[Governor of Virginia|Virginia Governor]] [[Ralph Northam]] says that he will increase enforcement of masks and social distancing as cases in the [[Hampton Roads]] area spike. [https://www.pilotonline.com/government/virginia/vp-nw-coronavirus-northam-updates-0714-20200714-6xypy3vvnfaf7mzu4xieb6oi5y-story.html (''The Virginian-Pilot'')]
***[[Moderna]] is expected to start a late stage clinical trial at 87 study locations in the [[United States]] for its [[COVID-19 vaccine]] on July 27. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-moderna-phase3-idUSKCN24F231 (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
***[[France]] is expected to make [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic|masks]] compulsory in indoor public spaces. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-france-nationalday-macron-covid-idUSKCN24F1DZ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***The number of COVID-19 cases in [[Venezuela]] surpasses 10,000. [https://apnews.com/350ebf6d5c00d519cb16cd70f0da6983 (AP)]
*[[Mongolia]] puts five districts under a six-day quarantine after a 15-year-old boy dies of the [[bubonic plague]] in the remote [[Gobi-Altai]] province amid fears of an epidemic. [https://english.alarabiya.net/en/News/world/2020/07/14/15-year-old-boy-dies-of-bubonic-plague-in-Mongolia-amid-outbreak-fears.html (AFP via Al Arabiya)]

;International relations 
*[[China–United States relations]], [[2019–20 Hong Kong protests]]
**U.S. President [[Donald Trump]] signs legislation and an executive order that will "hold China accountable" for recent "oppressive actions" in [[Hong Kong]] by ending its preferential economic status with the United States. [https://apnews.com/f160b6dd3b6bb73bfa5556ec9348edfd (AP)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-hongkong-security-trump/trump-ends-hong-kong-preferential-status-citing-oppressive-beijing-actions-against-city-idUSKCN24F2KQ (Reuters)]

;Law and crime
*[[Capital punishment]]
**[[Capital punishment in the United States]]
***The [[Supreme Court of the United States]] rules 5–4 to lift the block on four federal executions scheduled for July and August. Convicted murderer [[Daniel Lewis Lee]], whose execution was scheduled for the previous afternoon, is executed by lethal injection at the [[United States Penitentiary, Terre Haute|federal penitentiary]] in [[Terre Haute, Indiana]]. Two more executions are scheduled for later in the week. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national/daniel-lewis-lee-execution-terre-haute-supreme-court/2020/07/14/18e3bf20-c5c7-11ea-b037-f9711f89ee46_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Capital punishment in Iran]], [[2019–2020 Iranian protests]]
***Following a social media campaign that generated 7.5 million posts with the [[hashtag]] #do_not_execute, the Iranian authorities halt the impending executions of three anti-government protestors who were arrested during [[Mahshahr massacre|street protests in November 2019]] in which hundreds of demonstrators were killed. A retrial is ordered. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-53417228 (BBC News)] 
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Kentucky]]
***Nearly 100 people protesting the police killing of [[Shooting of Breonna Taylor|Breonna Taylor]] are arrested outside the home of [[Attorney General of Kentucky|Kentucky Attorney General]] [[Daniel Cameron (Kentucky politician)|Daniel Cameron]]. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/nearly-100-breonna-taylor-protesters-arrested-kentucky-attorney-general-s-n1233848 (NBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 United States elections]]
**[[2020 United States Senate elections]]
***People in [[2020 United States Senate election in Maine|Maine]], [[2020 United States Senate election in Alabama|Alabama]], and [[2020 United States Senate election in Texas|Texas]] are expected to cast their votes in both regular and run off primaries. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/14/politics/primary-elections-texas-alabama-maine/index.html (CNN)]
***Former [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn football]] coach [[Tommy Tuberville]] defeats former [[United States Attorney General|attorney general]] [[Jeff Sessions]] in the [[Alabama]] Republican primary. Tuberville will face Democratic incumbent [[Doug Jones (politician)|Doug Jones]]. [https://www.vox.com/2020/7/14/21324520/tuberville-wins-gop-senate-primary-july-sessions (Vox)]
*[[July 2020 New Zealand National Party leadership election]]
**[[Todd Muller]] resigns as leader of the [[New Zealand National Party]] citing health and family reasons. A party caucus elects [[Judith Collins]] as the party's new leader. [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300056130/todd-muller-resigns-as-leader-of-the-national-party (Stuff)] [https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300056981/judith-collins-the-new-leader-of-national-party-promises-to-crush-the-government (Stuff<sub>2</sub>)]
*[[2020 Belarusian presidential election]]
**The [[Belarus]]ian election commission bars two prominent opposition candidates to current [[President of Belarus|President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] from running in the election, ensuring a victory for Lukashenko. The barred candidates are [[Viktar Babaryka]] who was disqualified for an open criminal case against him and [[Valery Tsepkalo]] whose signatures on a supporting petition were nullified. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-belarus-election/two-main-challengers-to-belarus-president-barred-from-election-ballot-idUSKCN24F10W?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Hong Kong pro-democracy primaries]]
**[[Exit poll]]s results show a strong support for young [[pro-democracy]] candidates, including independent activist [[Joshua Wong]] and [[League of Social Democrats]] candidate [[Jimmy Sham]]. A spokesperson for the Liaison Office of China in Hong Kong says that the election could be in violation of the new security law and could be nullified. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20200714_35/ (NHK-World)]
*[[International student|International students in the United States]]
**The [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] reverses its [[travel visa|student visa]] policy, announced on July 6, to deport international students whose courses move fully online. The plan met stiff opposition. At least 59 [[University|universities]] and the [[State attorney general|attorneys general]] of 18 states sued to block this directive. Federal district judge [[Allison Burroughs]] dismisses the first case brought to court as [[Mootness|moot]] because the federal government has agreed to rescind the policy. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-53410285# (BBC News)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2020/07/14/trump-ice-college-student-visa-rule-online-classes-fall-2020/5437654002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport|UK Digital Media minister]] [[Oliver Dowden]] announces to the [[House of Commons]] that the country's [[Telecommunications in the United Kingdom|mobile providers]] will be barred from buying [[5G]] equipment from [[Huawei]] starting December 31, and will be required to remove it from their networks by 2027. [[John Browne, Baron Browne of Madingley|Lord Browne]] resigned from his position as chairman of Huawei's UK branch shortly before the announcement. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-53403793 (BBC News)]
